Tests of cumulative incidence functions

Source: vignettes/v3_gray_extensions.Rmd
v3_gray_extensions.Rmd

ciftest() compares survival or cumulative incidence curves between groups using a formula interface. For competing-risk outcomes, it provides the classical Gray test, score and augmented score tests, and tests combining multiple Fleming–Harrington (FH) temporal-weight directions. Use the Ditzhaus test for a quadratic statistic or MaxCombo for a maximum standardized score.

This vignette focuses on test selection, function calls, and interpreting ciftest() output. For a complete analysis with CIF estimation and risk ratios, see Worked examples.

Run a single CIF comparison with ciftest()

In diabetes.complications, epsilon denotes diabetic retinopathy (1), a competing macrovascular event (2), or censoring (0). The formula’s right-hand side identifies the groups. The variable fruitq1 compares the lowest fruit-intake quartile with the other quartiles. The event of interest defaults to code.event1 = 1.

library(cifmodeling)
data(diabetes.complications)

Request the classical Gray test with test = "gray":

fit_gray <- ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  test = "gray"
)
fit_gray
## 
## Gray's test
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Test: gray
## FH weights: rho = 0, gamma = 0
## Analysis strata: pooled
## Censoring strata: not used by this test
## Working AJ strata: not used by this test
## Variance: gray
## 
## Chi-squared = 8.8786, df = 1, p-value = 0.002885
generics::tidy(fit_gray)
##   statistic     p.value parameter      method   outcome.type test     weight
## 1  8.878578 0.002885361         1 Gray's test competing-risk gray unweighted
##   iteration fixed.point.residual   n
## 1         0                   NA 978

To fit the augmented score test, change test to "augmented". This procedure uses working models for event and censoring distributions when constructing the score and its variance:

fit_aug <- ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  test = "augmented"
)
fit_aug
## 
## Closed-form augmented Fine-Gray score test
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Test: augmented
## FH weights: rho = 0, gamma = 0
## Analysis strata: pooled
## Censoring strata: pooled
## Working AJ strata: fruitq1 only (2 fitted cells)
## Iteration: 0 (closed-form augmentation)
## Variance: score-iid
## 
## Chi-squared = 7.931, df = 1, p-value = 0.004859
generics::tidy(fit_aug)
##   statistic     p.value parameter                                     method
## 1   7.93102 0.004859441         1 Closed-form augmented Fine-Gray score test
##     outcome.type      test     weight iteration fixed.point.residual   n
## 1 competing-risk augmented unweighted         0                   NA 978

Both fitted objects contain statistic, parameter (degrees of freedom), p.value, and method. Use generics::tidy() to collect these fields in a data frame. The p-value concerns differences between CIFs over follow-up, not a risk ratio at a fixed time. Because Gray and augmented tests use different scores and covariance estimators, their p-values may differ; neither test is uniformly more powerful.

By default, test = "auto" selects the augmented score test for competing risks and the log-rank test for survival outcomes. Use test = "gray" when you specifically want the classical Gray test. These tests compare groups but do not, by themselves, establish causal effects.

Select early or late weighting

To emphasize differences early or late in follow-up, ciftest() accepts FH temporal weights of the form

w(t)={1−F1(t−)}ρF1(t−)γ, w(t)=\{1-F_1(t-)\}^{\rho}F_1(t-)^{\gamma},

Here, F1(t−)F_1(t-) is the left-limit CIF used to construct the weight. Larger ρ\rho emphasizes earlier differences, while larger γ\gamma emphasizes later differences. The estimated weight process depends on the component test: Gray and augmented score tests need not use the same estimated CIF. Inspect the process used in a fit through fit$diagnostics$fh.weight.process.

For competing-risk outcomes, test = "early" and test = "late" select augmented score tests with FH(1,0) and FH(0,1), respectively:

fit_early <- ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  test = "early"
)
fit_late <- ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  test = "late"
)
fit_early
## 
## Closed-form augmented Fine-Gray score test
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Test: augmented
## FH weights: rho = 1, gamma = 0
## Analysis strata: pooled
## Censoring strata: pooled
## Working AJ strata: fruitq1 only (2 fitted cells)
## Iteration: 0 (closed-form augmentation)
## Variance: score-iid
## 
## Chi-squared = 8.0774, df = 1, p-value = 0.004482
fit_late
## 
## Closed-form augmented Fine-Gray score test
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Test: augmented
## FH weights: rho = 0, gamma = 1
## Analysis strata: pooled
## Censoring strata: pooled
## Working AJ strata: fruitq1 only (2 fitted cells)
## Iteration: 0 (closed-form augmentation)
## Variance: score-iid
## 
## Chi-squared = 4.9028, df = 1, p-value = 0.02681

To use a different direction, specify rho and gamma alongside the test, for example, test = "augmented", rho = 2, gamma = 0. FH(0,0) is called "unweighted" because no additional temporal weight is applied; this does not mean that censoring adjustment is omitted. The terms "early" and "late" describe when differences are emphasized, not which group has the higher CIF.

Combine directions with the Ditzhaus test

test = "ditzhaus" (or "d") runs a quadratic-form test. For competing-risk outcomes, the default combines augmented scores with FH(0,0), FH(0,1), and FH(2,0) weights to give one omnibus p-value.

fit_ditzhaus <- ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  test = "ditzhaus"
)
fit_ditzhaus
## 
## Multiple-direction Closed-form augmented Fine-Gray score test (asymptotic chi-square)
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Component test: augmented
## Directions: unweighted (0, 0), FH01 (0, 1), early (2, 0)
## 
## Chi-squared = 8.5265, df = 3, p-value = 0.0363
generics::tidy(fit_ditzhaus)
##   statistic   p.value parameter
## 1  8.526544 0.0362953         3
##                                                                                  method
## 1 Multiple-direction Closed-form augmented Fine-Gray score test (asymptotic chi-square)
##     outcome.type      test directions   n
## 1 competing-risk augmented          3 978
fit_ditzhaus$directions
##    direction rho gamma
## 1 unweighted   0     0
## 2       FH01   0     1
## 3      early   2     0

ciftest() combines the scores into a quadratic-form statistic:

Q=U⊤V+U. Q=U^\top V^+U.

The fitted object stores the score vector UU in fit_ditzhaus$score and its covariance matrix VV in fit_ditzhaus$vcov.score. The test uses the generalized inverse V+V^+ and a chi-squared reference distribution with degrees of freedom equal to the numerical rank of VV. Consequently, three directions need not yield three degrees of freedom. fit_ditzhaus$directions records the FH weights, and fit_ditzhaus$components contains the individual fits. This omnibus statistic does not estimate a risk difference or ratio.

The "early" and "late" presets within directions use FH(2,0) and FH(0,2). These differ from the single-direction shortcuts test = "early" and test = "late". For custom weights, use directions and, if necessary, component.test:

fit_custom <- ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  component.test = "augmented",
  directions = rbind(
    early = c(rho = 1, gamma = 0),
    late  = c(rho = 0, gamma = 1)
  )
)
fit_custom
## 
## Multiple-direction Closed-form augmented Fine-Gray score test (asymptotic chi-square)
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Component test: augmented
## Directions: early (1, 0), late (0, 1)
## 
## Chi-squared = 8.0954, df = 2, p-value = 0.01746

Supplying directions alone selects the Ditzhaus test. For competing risks, the default component test is "augmented"; set component.test = "gray" or "score" to change the score and covariance calculation. For survival outcomes, you can use component.test = "logrank".

Run MaxCombo with test = "maxcombo"

For two groups with competing risks, test = "maxcombo" (or "m") combines augmented scores using FH(0,0), FH(2,0), and FH(0,1) by default. Supply directions to change the weights. The default two-sided test uses the largest absolute standardized score and a joint normal reference.

fit_maxcombo <- ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  test = "m",
  code.exposure.ref = 0
)
fit_maxcombo
## 
## MaxCombo augmented score test (joint normal reference)
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Component test: augmented
## Directions: unweighted (0, 0), early (2, 0), FH01 (0, 1)
## 
## Comparison: 1 vs 0, alternative = two.sided
## Standardized scores: unweighted = 2.8162, early = 2.8371, FH01 = 2.2142
## Max Z = 2.8371, p-value = 0.008381

For a prespecified lower CIF in the comparison group, set alternative = "less". Use "greater" for a higher CIF. code.exposure.ref selects the reference group by its code or factor level. The default is the first factor level present in the analysis data. The returned comparison identifies the two groups.

ciftest(
  Event(t, epsilon) ~ fruitq1,
  data = diabetes.complications,
  outcome.type = "competing-risk",
  test = "maxcombo",
  alternative = "less",
  code.exposure.ref = 0
)
## 
## MaxCombo augmented score test (joint normal reference)
## 
## Outcome: competing-risk
## Component test: augmented
## Directions: unweighted (0, 0), early (2, 0), FH01 (0, 1)
## 
## Comparison: 1 vs 0, alternative = less
## Standardized scores: unweighted = 2.8162, early = 2.8371, FH01 = 2.2142
## Max Z = -2.2142, p-value = 0.9955

Choosing a test

Use this table to select a ciftest() option:

Goal Call or result What you obtain
Standard survival-curve comparison ciftest(..., outcome.type = "survival", test = "auto") Log-rank test
Classical CIF comparison ciftest(..., test = "gray") Gray test statistic and p-value
Augmented CIF comparison (default) ciftest(..., test = "augmented") Augmented score test and p-value
Unaugmented score test ciftest(..., test = "score") Score test using the null-score IID variance
Focus on an earlier or later difference ciftest(..., test = "early") or "late" Single-direction FH-weighted test
Combine directions in a quadratic form ciftest(..., test = "ditzhaus") or directions = ... Omnibus quadratic statistic, rank-based df, p-value
Use the largest signed or absolute standardized score ciftest(..., test = "maxcombo", alternative = ...) MaxCombo statistic and global p-value

These options test related but distinct alternatives. For confirmatory analyses, prespecify the test and weight directions; choosing the smallest p-value after inspecting the data does not preserve the nominal significance level. The built-in Ditzhaus test uses an asymptotic chi-squared reference. Ditzhaus and Friedrich (2020) studied permutation calibration for weighted log-rank combinations. See Worked examples for a simpler comparison using this dataset and Function reference for the full argument list.

References

  • Gray RJ (1988). A class of K-sample tests for comparing the cumulative incidence of a competing risk. The Annals of Statistics, 16, 1141–1154.
  • Ditzhaus M, Friedrich S (2020). More powerful logrank permutation tests for two-sample survival data. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation, 90, 2209–2227. doi:10.1080/00949655.2020.1773463.
